sources.title: Schleswig-Holstein State Archives: The settlement of 1773
sources.note: Direct archive exhibition by Martin Rackwitz, 2023, PDF pages 1 to 3: territorial settlement, Kiel ceremony, canal and agricultural reforms. Canal length figures not used because publications count different sections.

sources.title: Society for Schleswig-Holstein History: Life around 1800
sources.note: Direct historical society article, sections Die Aufklärung and Die Leibeigenen werden frei. German writing is a quotation transcribed by the society from the December 1804 ordinance, not a newly inspected original sheet.

sources.title: City of Kiel: The canal warehouse
sources.note: Direct/indexed municipal interpretation: works 1777 to 1784, six locks, three warehouses, Holtenau warehouse 1780 to 1783.

sources.title: Municipality of Quarnbek: Landwehr ferry chronicle
sources.note: Indexed original municipal magazine, printed page 17: canal interrupted crossing, Dutch-style drawbridge, horse station and towpath. Narrow local account used for horses only, without universal claims about labor or towpath dimensions.

sources.title: Kiel University: History of the university
sources.note: Direct university history: foundation October 5, 1665, privileges of jurisdiction and taxation, removal in April and June 1867. Foundation is earlier background, not an event within the imported period.

sources.title: Kiel University: The development of its clinics
sources.note: Direct/indexed Martin Geist, October 19, 2019: university acquired Weber clinic in 1802, bedside teaching and research. The English introduction contains an apparent before/after mistranslation, which is not repeated.

sources.title: Kiel City Archives: Kiel’s water supply
sources.note: Direct Christa Geckeler, February 12, 2012: hollowed tree pipes, Schmidt bequest 1821, private outlets/public water collection, wells near latrines, Schreventeich transfer 1862 and works 1863. No claim untreated water was safe.

sources.title: Kiel City Archives: The Altona to Kiel railway
sources.note: Indexed original city archive chronology: works began March 1843, 333 bridges and culverts, scheduled trains September 9, 1844, ceremony September 18. Distinguishes public service from official inauguration.

sources.title: Schleswig-Holstein State Archives: Prussian administration
sources.note: Direct archive classification history: wars of 1864 and 1866, formal incorporation patent January 12, 1867, provincial administration and limited self-government.

sources.title: Schleswig-Holstein State Archives: Becoming a Prussian province
sources.note: Indexed original state archive exhibition: January 24, 1867 ceremony, hopes for Friedrich VIII, emigration to avoid three-year military service. Public copy labels this as life after the duchy’s annexation.

sources.title: Leibniz Institute of European History: Mecklenburg-Schwerin
sources.note: Direct academic historical GIS state entry: partition 1701, elevation 1815, constitutional history, abdication November 14, 1918 and 1920 republican constitution. Geometry warning is independent inspection of imported polygons.

sources.title: Carina Freitag: Mecklenburg-Schwerin’s parliamentary government
sources.note: Direct University of Rostock dissertation, 2010, printed pages 49 to 51 (PDF indices 68 to 70): estate representation, 1849 constitution, reversal September 1850. No claim nineteenth-century representative institutions were universal democracy.

sources.title: Schwerin Open-Air Museum: The history of Mueß village
sources.note: Direct municipal museum account: inherited farms and younger siblings in eighteenth/nineteenth-century development, smallholder plots three to nine hectares, 1857 eleven Büdner growing rye/oats/potatoes. Twentieth-century livestock data not projected backward.

sources.title: Schwerin Open-Air Museum: Mueß gardens and old crops
sources.note: Direct municipal museum account: reconstructed ideal teacher’s garden based on E. Gang’s 1888 articles/plans; Kröger family climbing bean documented since 1850 and donated to museum in 1997. Later recollection is not presented as an original nineteenth-century writing sample.

sources.title: German Foundation for Monument Protection: Ludwigslust’s papier-mâché
sources.note: Direct 2012 conservation article: mold materials and production, 1773 order to recycle official records, surviving writing on object backs, factory active into early nineteenth century. Secret composition not asserted known.

sources.title: Mecklenburg-Vorpommern Parliament: History of Schwerin Castle
sources.note: Direct official architectural history: court returned 1837, Demmler/Stüler, reconstruction completed 1857 and Chambord model. Earlier court-move dates conflict in regional accounts and are omitted.

sources.title: Deutschlandmuseum: Founding the seaside resort of Heiligendamm
sources.note: Direct museum calendar: bathhouse opened September 21, 1793, physician’s bathing rules and affluent visitors. Historical therapeutic belief described, not endorsed as present-day medical advice.

sources.title: University of Greifswald: Digitized works of Fritz Reuter
sources.note: Direct scholarly bibliography: Läuschen un Rimels, collected works volume 1, seventh edition, Wismar Hinstorff 1864. Exact title checked in catalog, linked edition scan not accessed. First edition 1853 Altentreptow also catalogued here.

sources.title: Fritz Reuter Literature Museum: First works, Läuschen un Rimels
sources.note: Museum-owned English audio transcript, station12, directly read by root. Confirms title meaning,1853self-publication financed by friends,Fritz/Luise packing and shipping,and1200copies sold out. Researcher had checked German indexed version; root direct German fetch failed, so public link uses accessible English counterpart of the same museum work.

sources.title: University of Greifswald: Fritz Reuter biography
sources.note: Direct university teaching biography, four pages: Stavenhagen origin and residence in Treptow from 1850. Used to distinguish regional author and publishing network from exclusive territorial residence.

proposedOverrides.summary: A northern German duchy and later grand duchy, with estate government, farming villages, seaside bathing and Low German literature; its monarchy ended in 1918.

batchIdentityNotes.note: Decoded imported 1783 to 1878 bbox 8.7787,53.503 to 11.0719,54.3723. Late duchy under Danish crown, not ancient Holstein or the whole modern federal state. Formal Prussian annexation January 1867 is public; imported final years continue under successor administration. No unsupported immediate 1864 partition into Austria/Prussia repeated.

Decoded 1783 to 1878. Earlier bbox 10.7551,52.6184 to 13.8043,54.2545 extends through Mecklenburg-Strelitz; public warning included. 1815 footprint bbox 10.7551,52.8929 to 13.2895,54.2545. Does not alias Strelitz. Actual political narrative 1701 partition to 1918 monarchy; 1888 garden source and 1997 seed preservation explicitly later. No midpoint years for broad village practices.
